verses.text: Come, let us sing for joy to the LORD; let us shout to the Rock of our salvation!

xrefs.text: and drank the same spiritual drink; for they drank from the spiritual rock that accompanied them, and that rock was Christ.
For the choirmaster. According to Gittith. Of Asaph. Sing for joy to God our strength; make a joyful noise to the God of Jacob.
Let everything that has breath praise the LORD! Hallelujah!
The LORD lives, and blessed be my Rock! And may God, the Rock of my salvation, be exalted—
Sing to the LORD a new song; sing to the LORD, all the earth.

verses.text: Let us enter His presence with thanksgiving; let us make a joyful noise to Him in song.

xrefs.text: Speak to one another with psalms, hymns, and spiritual songs. Sing and make music in your hearts to the Lord,
Enter His gates with thanksgiving and His courts with praise; give thanks to Him and bless His name.
Sing to Him, sing praises to Him; tell of all His wonders.

They will come and shout for joy on the heights of Zion; they will be radiant over the bounty of the LORD— the grain, new wine, and oil, and the young of the flocks and herds. Their life will be like a well-watered garden, and never again will they languish.
With what shall I come before the LORD when I bow before the God on high? Should I come to Him with burnt offerings, with year-old calves?

verses.text: For the LORD is a great God, a great King above all gods.

xrefs.text: For great is the LORD, and greatly to be praised; He is to be feared above all gods.
There is none like You, O LORD. You are great, and Your name is mighty in power.
Great is the LORD and greatly to be praised; His greatness is unsearchable.
For You, O LORD, are Most High over all the earth; You are exalted far above all gods.
For I know that the LORD is great; our Lord is above all gods.

verses.text: In His hand are the depths of the earth, and the mountain peaks belong to Him.

xrefs.text: The LORD does all that pleases Him in the heavens and on the earth, in the seas and in all their depths.
He stood and measured the earth; He looked and startled the nations; the ancient mountains crumbled; the perpetual hills collapsed. His ways are everlasting.
The mountains saw You and quaked; torrents of water swept by. The deep roared with its voice and lifted its hands on high.
The mountains quake before Him, and the hills melt away; the earth trembles at His presence— the world and all its dwellers.
The mountains will melt beneath Him, and the valleys will split apart, like wax before the fire, like water rushing down a slope.

verses.text: The sea is His, for He made it, and His hands formed the dry land.

xrefs.text: And God said, “Let the waters under the sky be gathered into one place, so that the dry land may appear.” And it was so.
when He set a boundary for the sea, so that the waters would not surpass His command, when He marked out the foundations of the earth.
He piles up the waters of the sea; He puts the depths into storehouses.
“I am a Hebrew,” replied Jonah. “I worship the LORD, the God of the heavens, who made the sea and the dry land.”
when I fixed its boundaries and set in place its bars and doors,

verses.text: O come, let us worship and bow down; let us kneel before the LORD our Maker.

xrefs.text: that at the name of Jesus every knee should bow, in heaven and on earth and under the earth,
Know that the LORD is God. It is He who made us, and we are His; we are His people, and the sheep of His pasture.
Come, let us sing for joy to the LORD; let us shout to the Rock of our salvation!
... for this reason I bow my knees before the Father,
you were bought at a price. Therefore glorify God with your body.

verses.text: For He is our God, and we are the people of His pasture, the sheep under His care. Today, if you hear His voice,

xrefs.text: God again designated a certain day as “Today, when a long time later He spoke through David as was just stated: “Today, if you hear His voice, do not harden your hearts.”
As it has been said: “Today, if you hear His voice, do not harden your hearts, as you did in the rebellion.”
Behold, I stand at the door and knock. If anyone hears My voice and opens the door, I will come in and dine with him, and he with Me.
I am the good shepherd. I know My sheep and My sheep know Me,
Therefore, as the Holy Spirit says: “Today, if you hear His voice,

verses.text: do not harden your hearts as you did at Meribah, in the day at Massah in the wilderness,

xrefs.text: He named the place Massah and Meribah because the Israelites quarreled, and because they tested the LORD, saying, “Is the LORD among us or not?”
do not harden your hearts, as you did in the rebellion, in the day of testing in the wilderness,
These were the waters of Meribah, where the Israelites quarreled with the LORD, and He showed His holiness among them.
And the LORD said to Moses, “How long will this people treat Me with contempt? How long will they refuse to believe in Me, despite all the signs I have performed among them?
As it has been said: “Today, if you hear His voice, do not harden your hearts, as you did in the rebellion.”

verses.text: where your fathers tested and tried Me, though they had seen My work.

xrefs.text: not one of the men who have seen My glory and the signs I performed in Egypt and in the wilderness— yet have tested Me and disobeyed Me these ten times—
We should not test Christ, as some of them did, and were killed by snakes.
But they tested and disobeyed God Most High, for they did not keep His decrees.
How often they disobeyed Him in the wilderness and grieved Him in the desert!
But they continued to sin against Him, rebelling in the desert against the Most High.

verses.text: For forty years I was angry with that generation, and I said, “They are a people whose hearts go astray, and they have not known My ways.”

xrefs.text: And with whom was God angry for forty years? Was it not with those who sinned, whose bodies fell in the wilderness?
where your fathers tested and tried Me, and for forty years saw My works.
“How long, O simple ones, will you love your simple ways? How long will scoffers delight in their scorn and fools hate knowledge?
Why, O LORD, do You make us stray from Your ways and harden our hearts from fearing You? Return, for the sake of Your servants, the tribes of Your heritage.
He endured their conduct for about forty years in the wilderness.

verses.text: So I swore on oath in My anger, “They shall never enter My rest.”

xrefs.text: Now we who have believed enter that rest. As for the others, it is just as God has said: “So I swore on oath in My anger, ‘They shall never enter My rest.’” And yet His works have been finished since the foundation of the world.
not one will ever see the land that I swore to give their fathers. None of those who have treated Me with contempt will see it.
And again, as He says in the passage above: “They shall never enter My rest.
So I swore on oath in My anger, ‘They shall never enter My rest.’”
And to whom did He swear that they would never enter His rest? Was it not to those who disobeyed?
